why: Historical schema size comparison, not model usage or billing. Legacy approx_tokens_per_turn fields mean schema_bytes/4 estimates. Loaded, cached and billed tokens were not measured. Native filters and deferred discovery change the actual surface.

servers.schema_bytes_note: Sum of the 31 per-tool byte counts. Measure-McpSchemaCost.ps1 also reports the serialized tools ARRAY at 163,991 -- 32 bytes more, the JSON framing between entries. Subset costs (see CATALOG.json mcp_tool_budget) can only be derived by summing per-tool bytes, so the sum is the basis every figure in this pack uses. Quoting both is how a restated number drifts.
servers.note: The largest recorded schema in this comparison. No actual context occupancy or billing was measured. Three dedicated creation/NIF/placement tools (housecarl_create, housecarl_nif_set, housecarl_place) are 35,458 bytes, 22% of the total and more than the whole of Skyrim Forge. Its capability is genuinely irreplaceable (live MO2 load-order truth, conflict trees, keyless Nexus), which is exactly why it belongs in a scoped profile rather than the always-on core.
servers.scope: Hermes 'skyrim' profile and per-project capability profiles only. Never always-on.

servers.note: SEVEN more tools than houseCARL for a tenth of the context. Typed, narrow parameter schemas rather than deep nested record objects. Forge also has a CLI, so the MCP surface is a convenience rather than the only access path -- which is why it stays out of the default profiles even though it is cheap.
servers.scope: Not a default profile member. Reachable through its skill and CLI; -WithForgeCompatibility connects the MCP explicitly.

servers.note: Measured in v7.9.9. Keyless, exactly 2 of the 25 tools work, and both duplicate a native provider capability. See firecrawl-mcp.json for the per-tool capability matrix.

conclusion: A server is not expensive because it has many tools; it is expensive because its schemas are large. Ranking by tool count would have put Skyrim Forge (52) ahead of houseCARL (45) as the thing to cut, and that is backwards by an order of magnitude. Measure before deciding, and scope the expensive ones to the projects that need them instead of removing capability.
